knowledge:
- key_parameters: bamfiles=Character vector of paths to BAM files containing Ribo-meth-seq alignments ;; fasta=Path to the genomic or transcriptomic FASTA reference file ;; gff=Path to the GFF3/GTF annotation file ;; model=The machine learning model (e.g., Random Forest) used for predicting modification sites
- alternatives: `rnamodr` (standard ratio-based detection) which is preferred when machine learning models are not trained for the specific organism or when simpler threshold-based scoring (Score A, B, C) is sufficient.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have Ribo-meth-seq data and want to leverage machine learning classifiers to identify 2'-O-methylations with potentially higher accuracy than traditional ratio-based methods.
- pitfalls: Applying pre-trained models to datasets with significantly different sequencing depths, library preparation protocols, or from different species without retraining or validation can lead to high false-positive or false-negative rates.

workflows.name: detect_2_o_methylations_ml
workflows.intent: Detect 2'-O-methylations from Ribo-meth-seq BAM files using machine learning classifiers.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and define input file paths ;; 2. Initialize the ModMLRiboMethSeq modifier object ;; 3. Extract predicted 2'-O-methylations using the modifications function
workflows.code:
library(rnamodr.ml)
bamfiles <- c("sample1.bam", "sample2.bam")
fasta <- "genome.fa"
gff <- "annotation.gff"
mod <- ModMLRiboMethSeq(bamfiles, fasta = fasta, gff = gff)
mods <- modifications(mod)
